title: New vs old income-tax regime — which one to pick
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: India has two income-tax regimes. The new regime is the default: lower slab rates, a standard deduction of ₹75,000 for salaried people, and a Section 87A rebate that makes tax zero for taxable income up to ₹12 lakh (so up to about ₹12.75 lakh of salary), but it allows almost no deductions like 80C, 80D or HRA. The old regime has higher slab rates but lets you claim deductions: 80C (₹1.5 lakh), 80D health insurance, HRA, home-loan interest, NPS extra ₹50,000 and more. There is no single deduction number that works for everyone — it depends on salary. On a salary up to about ₹12.75 lakh the new regime means zero tax, so it always wins. Above that, the old regime only wins if your deductions beyond the standard deduction are large: roughly ₹5.4 lakh at a ₹15 lakh salary, ₹6.4 lakh at ₹18 lakh, ₹7.1 lakh at ₹20 lakh, and about ₹8 lakh at ₹25 lakh or more (80C ₹1.5 lakh + 80D + NPS ₹50,000 + home-loan interest ₹2 lakh + HRA all together). If you have a big home loan, rent with HRA and many investments, run both numbers. Salaried people can switch every year; use the Tax tab in Artha Kavach to compare both regimes on your salary.
summary_hinglish: New regime default hai: slab rates kam, ₹75,000 standard deduction aur ₹12 lakh taxable income tak 87A rebate se zero tax, par 80C/80D/HRA jaise deductions nahi. Old regime mein rates zyada hain par deductions milte hain. Deductions kam hain to new regime aam taur par better; Tax tab mein dono compare kar lo.
summary_hi: नया टैक्स रिजीम डिफ़ॉल्ट है: कम स्लैब दरें, ₹75,000 स्टैंडर्ड डिडक्शन और ₹12 लाख तक की टैक्सेबल आय पर 87A रिबेट से शून्य टैक्स, पर 80C/80D/HRA जैसी कटौतियां नहीं। पुराने रिजीम में दरें ज़्यादा हैं पर कटौतियां मिलती हैं। कटौतियां कम हों तो नया रिजीम आम तौर पर बेहतर है।
